content.title: How UConn held off Illinois in the Final Four to advance to men's NCAA Tournament championship game
content.text: SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMonday night's odds Getty Images Both Michigan and UConn got off to hot starts in Saturday’s Final Four games. The Huskies had to endure a push from Illinois while the Wolverines ran away from Arizona. Considering Michigan’s dominant play, it’s no surprise the Wolverines are big favorites for Monday’s national championship game.Michigan is favored by 7.5 points on DraftKings, BetMGM and FanDuel. The Wolverines opened as a 6.5-point favorite on FanDuel, but that number quickly moved so that all three sportsbooks showed matching odds.First look at Monday night Getty Images The stage is set. UConn and Michigan will play for the national championship in men’s basketball on Monday night in Indianapolis.The No. 2-seeded Huskies, seeking a third title in four seasons, dispatched No. seed 3 Illinois 71-62. Top-seeded Michigan routed fellow No. 1 Arizona 91-73, adding a fourth blowout win to its five-game run through this NCAA Tournament.The results on Saturday ensured a historic result in the title game. No program has won three championships in four years since John Wooden’s UCLA teams more than years ago. And it’s been longer than a quarter-century since a Big Ten team — Michigan State in 2000 — hoisted the trophy.Hurley on AuriemmaSpeaking with a group of reporters Saturday after his UConn men’s basketball team beat Illinois to advance to the national championship game, coach Dan Hurley offered words of support for Geno Auriemma, who coaches the UConn women’s team.Auriemma shocked many observers with his outburst near the end of his team’s 62-48 loss to South Carolina in Friday night’s semifinal game. As time expired, Auriemma got into an argument with South Carolina coach Dawn Staley in the handshake line before storming off the court without his team.Hurley is known for his hot-headedness and recently went viral for staring down and butting heads with a referee after UConn guard Braylon Mullins’ game-winning 3-pointer in an Elite Eight win over Duke.“Obviously, I’ve had a negative influence on Geno,” Hurley said, eliciting laughter. “And it’s crazy, because Geno’s helped me so much,” Hurley continued. “The way he handled the whole thing, such a stand-up guy, with the way he handled it with the statement, and he’s one of the classiest people.”Underwood gets emotional Getty ImagesBrad Underwood is full of emotion talking postgame.💬 “This team, like I said, gave me joy because they were about all the right things. If you want to put a contest together about good human beings, we’ll win. There’s no question what this group will be in life. As a coach, that’s why I got in this. Am I competitive? Does today stink? It hurts. My gut hurts so bad right now that I feel for all of them.”“We’ve got great people. We’ve got great support. For that, I’ll reflect at some time. Today is not a very good time to ask me that. But I’ll reflect on what we’re doing. I feel sad. I’m sad. If you want to know the truth, I’m sad. … I’m going to steal a quote from Kelvin Sampson. I may not be as big a part of their life, but they are my life, and I’m sad.”Wagler on the Illini Getty ImagesKeaton Wagler on the Illini locker room postgame:💬 “There was a lot of emotions, a lot of tears. I think that’s just how hard we worked this whole year. You never want the season to end. That’s what it was. I think we had a really great season, a special season, making history. I love each and every one of my teammates, and I wouldn’t have wanted to do it with anyone else.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMore from Underwood Getty ImagesMore from Illinois head coach Brad Underwood:💬 “I’m really bad at the end of seasons, guys. I’m terrible. I’ve been doing this a long time, and I’ve never been around a group of guys who have given me more joy. We didn’t have bad practices. They played for the name on the front. Andrej (Stojakovic) came here with the intent of being around winning and being a part of that, and this young man has grown to a whole new level. I couldn’t be prouder of him.“I think they (Illinois fans) fell in love with this group because of who they are as people. It’s just an extremely high-character locker room. Endings stink. … today was not our day. I want them to all hold their head high and feel proud of the jersey they wore. I’m selfish here when I say this, the joy that they gave me this year was very, very meaningful.”Underwood on the loss Getty ImagesHere’s what Brad Underwood had to say to start Illinois’ news conference:“A lot of credit to UConn. They fight. They compete. Very, very good basketball team. Seemed like we were fighting uphill all day. I felt really good at half being down eight. They were 42 percent on twos. They banked one in.”“I liked our looks. Even though we were 3 of 14 from 3, I liked every one of our looks. I thought defensively it was the tempo that we wanted. I thought we were really solid.”“We fought, we fought, we fought, and had a very tough shooting night, especially at the rim. We missed some shots that we normally don’t miss. It’s part of this game. The ball has to go in. … I thought our looks were really good, and I wouldn’t do anything on that side over again.”More of your views on tonight's gameAnd here are what some of our readers on our Discuss tab had to say about UConn’s win: Getty ImagesDan Hurley on his program: 💬 “We’re a tough program. We’re a tough program. We’re a group of fighters. It’s not appealing to everyone. I’m sure there’s some people in here that it’s off-putting for. But we are a group of fighters. We are incredibly tough. We’ve got incredible will. We go into these games, we’re ready for battle.”Hurley on Demary Getty Images Dan Hurley was asked about Silas Demary Jr.'s critical offensive rebound that led to Braylon Mullins’ late 3. Hurley used it as a chance to reiterate his dissatisfaction with being tonight’s underdog:💬 “Yeah, we knew what it was. You’re coming into the game as an underdog versus a team that you beat by 13 points earlier in the season, which was kind of surprising, that that’s how we kind of came into the game.“Obviously I’ve been waiting to say that and now I forgot your question.”He then went on to actually answer the question.💬 “What he’s (Demary) done for our basketball team, the mentality, it was everything we were lacking last year, just a guard like him, ball hawk, incredible toughness, on the backboard. Made (Keaton) Wagler work for it, made (Kylan) Boswell, just his on ball defense. He’s a shell of himself offensively. He is really gutting it out, and the courage he has showed, I think, has been inspiring for the group.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementA reader's thoughts on UConn ... and Hurley Getty Images We’ve received an email from Robert Y. about UConn’s win over Illinois. Here’s what Robert had to say:UCONN had the better team and the better coach! Illinois took far too many shots beyond the 3-point line. Shot selection was poor throughout the game, and UCONN played excellent defense.Remember, you can share your thoughts on tonight’s Final Four action by sending us an email at live@theathletic.com.Reed remains reliable Getty Images The fact that Tarris Reed Jr. had only 17 points tonight says more about UConn inexplicably going away from him in the second half than it does his overall body of work. Reed turned in a 17-point, 11-rebound double-double on 6-of-12 shooting, and he went a perfect 5-of-5 from the line. His reward? A heavyweight matchup with the uber-talented frontcourt of either Arizona or Michigan.Mullins on opening 3-pointer Getty Images Braylon Mullins on his game-opening 3-pointer: 💬 “I think it was the flow of the game, but coming into the game, I knew I needed to shoot it with confidence coming off last Sunday, just to have that flow, boosts all the confidence for you to keep shooting within the game.”Wagler goes out strong Getty Images It will come as little solace for Keaton Wagler tonight when he learns he was the game’s leading scorer, with 20 points on 7-for-16 shooting in Illinois’ losing effort. Wagler struggled mightily from deep, going just 2-for-10 from 3-point range, but he showed the athleticism and finesse around the rim that make him such an exciting NBA Draft prospect. His performance tonight, despite the loss, gave plenty of flashes of the talent that will likely see him get his name called early in Brooklyn in June.More from Hurley Getty Images More from UConn head coach Dan Hurley on his team's win tonight over Illinois: 💬 “Couldn’t be more proud of my guys and how hard they fought when most people probably didn’t think we were going to win the game, or at least a little bit of what I saw on TV today, you know, TNT and some of the different prognostications.“So it was great to win the game. I had to throw some shade.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWelcome home, Braylon Mullins Getty Images Once again, Braylon Mullins was at the center of the action for UConn in the Huskies' return to the Final Four — a short drive from his hometown in Indiana.Fresh off his already-iconic 3-pointer to beat Duke in the Elite Eight, Mullins got the scoring started in the game’s opening minutes and hit the de facto dagger in the game’s closing minutes — both, of course, via 3-pointers.Mullins finished with 15 points on just just 5-for-14 shooting from the field, but he was 4-for-7 from 3 and made those four makes count.UConn makes it hurt from deep Getty Images UConn only shot 35 percent from the field, just a hair better than Illinois' 34 percent shooting.But the Huskies took a larger-than-usual amound of 3s, 33, and made 12 of them for a 36 percent rate from deep. That was a major difference in this game, especially when factoring Illinois’ uncharacteristic poor shooting from beyond the arc.Pearl compares Hurley to coaching legend Getty Images Bruce Pearl: 💬 “Dan Hurley is doing stuff that John Wooden did.”Illinois struggled both times against UConn Illinois' two lowest point totals of the season came against UConn. Illini lost 74-61 to the Huskies back in November, and 71-62 in the Final Four. The Illini were held under 70 points only one other time this season: their 65-55 win over Houston in the Sweet 16.Hurley praises Mullins after UConn's win After Braylon Mullins’ interview, coach Dan Hurley and the freshman shared Hurley’s iconic head butt. Then Wolfson spoke with Hurley…On Mullins: 💬 “The start to the game, and the finish to the game — are they booing the head butt? I don’t know what they’re booing.”“But he’s (Mullins) amazing. He got us here, he got us off to a great start. You’re set up for success at UConn. Geno Auriemma, Jim Calhoun, Kevin Ollie, incredible coaches before me, got the best staff in the country, the best group of players. There’s nothing like the bus ride to the stadium on Monday night, over to the stadium, when you’re one of the last teams staaaanding!”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMullins says UConn is ready for national championship Getty Images Braylon Mullins to Tracy Wolfson: 💬 “Playing in front of all these fans, UConn always shows out. We’re so ready for the national championship game, this is what I came here to play for. Let’s get it on Monday.”Hurley unsure why fans are booing him Getty Images Dan Hurley💬 "Are they booing the headbutt? I don't know what they're booing."Hurley gets booed after Huskies' win Getty Images Dan Hurley is being BOOED during his postgame interview on the court. You have to assume he relishes these moments.UConn keeps rollingUConn will play for its third title in four years on Monday night as the program tries to become just the third in men's basketball to win at least seven national titles (UCLA and Kentucky are the other two with 11 and eight, respectively). So how did the Huskies keep winning in March and knock off Illinois? Our CJ Moore breaks down yet another UConn win in the Final Four here.UConn defense solves Illinois twice Getty Images Broadcast just said only twice this season Illinois has scored less than 65 points. Both against UConn.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementTough ending for Fighting Illini fans Illinois fans are understandably bummed as a special season ends in disappointment. All around the stadium you can see orange headed for the exits.Could Karaban join historic club? It should be noted the history that UConn is now chasing to become only the third men's program to win three titles in four years. The two previous to achieve the feat of winning three within a four-year span: UCLA (1964–1967, under John Wooden) and Kentucky (1948–1951, under Adolph Rupp).UConn's Alex Karaban is trying to become the first men's player in over five decades to win three championships in a college career.What a streak by UConn Getty Images UConn has won 19 straight games in the Sweet 16 or later, an unbelievable stat. The last such loss was the 2009 Final Four. It will play for yet another national title.Illinois went cold at worst time Getty Images The Illini entered the Final Four with one of the top offenses in the country. But they couldn't overcome their inability to make open 3s in a dome setting tonight.Illinois finished an ugly 6-for-25 from the 3-point range in this game.Huskies one win away from a dynasty Getty Images UConn advances to play for its third national championship in four years.What a run for Dan Hurley and the Huskies.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementOn Monday, UConn is gonna play for its third title in four years. Wow. Those are like, women's stats.UConn outlasts Illinois 71-62 Getty Images FINAL – UConn 71, Illinois 62Maybe it’s not the Huskies you thought would get there, but a UConn basketball team is headed to the national championship!In a tournament run of thrilling finishes, UConn gets another close game to fall its way late. The Huskies led nearly wire to wire and closed out the game with strong defensive play and clutch free throws. Tarris Reed Jr. led the Huskies with 17 points and 11 rebounds, while Elite Eight hero Braylon Mullins hit four of UConn’s 12 3-pointers in the win. Getty Images H2 0:26 – UConn 68, Illinois 62Silas Demary Jr. hits both of his free throws and the UConn lead boosts back to six points.Keaton Wagler misses a 3-pointer in response, and UConn grabs the rebound and takes the foul.I'm sure Duke fans are already having a tough time watching these games, but these UConn press breaks must be extra salt in the wound.A very impressive stat from the broadcast: Keaton Wagler and Braylon Mullins are the first pair of opposing freshmen with more than 15 points in a Final Four game, since Michael Jordan and Patrick Ewing. Don’t think there’s better company.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementThat Silas Demary Jr., offensive rebound should not be forgotten in the minutiae of this game. That gives him nine for the game, more than anyone on Illinois and second only to Tarris Reed Jr.'s 11. He also has a game-high seven assists. Getty Images The freshmen trade massive 3s, with Mullins and Wagler each hitting from deep. Illinois needs to get a turnover.Mullins shines in the clutchBraylon Mullins magnet ball in the clutch remains activated. Big answer by Keaton Wagler though. Keaton Wagler, who isn’t having a good day from deep, muscles his way into the paint for a critical two points for the Illini. He’s 1-for-7 from 3 but has still managed 17 points, 5-of-6 from two.That was Braylon Mullins’ first points of the entire second half.H2 0:43 – UConn 66, Illinois 62UConn misses a 3-pointer on its ensuing possession but collects the offensive rebound.After the Huskies burn time off the clock, Braylon Mullins drills a 3-pointer. Then, Keaton Wagler answers back with a 3-pointer of his own.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWagler cuts Illinois' deficit to 4 points Getty Images H2 1:38 – UConn 63, Illinois 59After UConn fails to make either of its shots off an inbound, Keaton Wagler attacks the rim and lays in a shot off the glass.Wagler's shot cuts the Illinois deficit to four points. To Ira's point: UConn's season-high is 34 3-point attempts in a game. Close with 2:08 left to play.Reed calls timeout to avoid turnoverGood, poised decision there by Reed. The double came and he had nowhere to go. UConn only has one timeout remaining though.UConn is 11-for-31 from beyond the arc, the Huskies’ most 3-pointers in a game since hitting 12 against Xavier on March 12.Illinois trails by 5 in final 3 minutesH2 2:46 – UConn 61, Illinois 56Illinois is refusing to go away. After UConn gets its offense going with a Tarris Reed Jr. layup and emphatic Solo Ball dunk, Ben Humrichous answers with a 3-pointer.We've got ourselves a game!SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Getty Images Why UConn chose not to go inside to Tarris Reed as long as it did, who knows?But the UConn big man snapped a loooong scoreless stretch for the Huskies, who are now clinging to a five-point lead with 2:46 left.No idea why Ben Humrichous shot that but it's hard to argue with the result. Cash.UConn’s 4:43-minute scoring drought has finally been watered.UConn hasn’t scored since Jaylin Stewart’s 3 at the 9:44 mark. We are now in the final five minutes. Getty Images (Final five minutes of games within six points):Arizona 14-2UConn 13-3Michigan 12-3Illinois 9-6SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUConn has not made a field goal since the 9:44 mark, a Jaylin Stewart triple that put the Huskies up by 14.The lead is now just four points.So much for Illinois having a monopoly on Slavic big men tonight.Brad Underwood is living and dying with each of these missed shots for the Illinois. They've duffed a couple at the rim during this 8-0 run that — which they've done mostly at the foul line, making no field goals in 3-plus minutes. Illinois is 4-for-8 on shots at the rim thus far.Illinois rallying despite shooting struggles Getty Images Sometimes it's just not your night. Illinois has seemed to have a lid on the rim all night. Illini shooting just 15-for-44 in the game.Those shots have not started falling on this Illini run, either. Illinois' last six points have all come at the free-throw line.Yeah that last call on Silas Demary was questionable to be kind. It's 20 fouls on UConn, 13 on Illinois, and yes, the Illini have done more driving and the Huskies more jump shooting. But that deficit feels larger than it should be.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Getty Images UConn needed that timeout desperately. A 14-point lead is now just six with just over six minutes to play. The Huskies offense has no rhythm right now.H2 6:08 – UConn 57, Illinois 51UConn takes a timeout with the Fighting Illini within six points.Illinois has made this a competitive game with a strong showing at the free-throw line in this half: 11-of-12 from the stripe. Free throws have accounted for 11 of Illinois’ 22 points this half, and those trips have put multiple UConn players in foul trouble.Whether or not those calls are questionable, Illinois has forged its comeback attempt by taking advantage of the UConn fouls.In comparison, six of UConn’s 20 points this half have come from free throws.The officiating calls are borderline laughable at this point.More questionable officiating Getty Images The foul calls are getting more questionable as we go which is certainly not what you want.H2 8:00 – UConn 57, Illinois 49An Illinois run trims the UConn lead to single digits, with the last four points coming on converted free-throw attempts.I’m interested to see the group the Huskies send back out onto the floor — could more starters be in the mix now with Illinois back within a couple of possessions?SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementSam Vecenie just looked it up: the UConn lineup Marks referenced — Malachi Smith, Jayden Ross, Solo Ball, Jaylin Stewart, and Eric Reibe — had played 12 minutes together all season entering this game. The Huskies just got three or four minutes from them and mostly survived, but Illinois' 6-0 run has cut its deficit to single digits. Getty Images To Michael's point, I feel confident in predicting one of two things is going to happen tonight. Either UConn will win this game, or Dan Hurley will go on an all-timer of a rant about the officiating.Illinois already at double bonus Getty Images There have been 16 fouls called over the first 12 minutes of this half. Illinois will be in the double bonus the rest of the way.The three behind him were Coach K, Roy Williams, and Billy Donovan. Quite the company Hurley is keeping.Putting Hurley's success in perspective Getty Images For those who need to be reminded of Dan Hurley’s success, the broadcast just showed his win percentage in the NCAA Tournament. Hurley is second to John Wooden, a monument of the sport, at .792 with a 19-5 record. Wooden went 47-10 in March during his dynasty at UCLA.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementH2 8:03 – UConn 57, Illinois 47A check-in on players in foul trouble:Malachi Smith, UConn: four foulsBraylon Mullins, UConn: three foulsEric Reibe, UConn: three foulsDavid Mirkovic, Illinois: three foulsYou can definitely tell which of these teams has more recent Final Four experience — and more recent experience shooting in a dome.Karaban, Ball lead UConn offense Getty Images H2 10:06 – UConn 54, Illinois 43After Tarris Reed Jr. and Braylon Mullins carried the UConn offense in the first half, Alex Karaban and Solo Ball are taking over in the second half.Karaban is a perfect 6-of-6 on free throws, while Ball has knocked down two 3-pointers and is almost in double figures in the second half alone. Getty Images Illinois’ largest deficit this year was 21 points twice — UConn in November and Michigan in February.UConn is currently running Malachi Smith, Jayden Ross, Solo Ball, Jaylin Stewart, and Eric Reibe. That, uh, is a lineup. Not one I expect Dan Hurley to rock with for long.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementBill Murray is getting booed by the Illinois fans and he is loving it, egging them on by putting his hands to his ears.Hurley veers close to technical foul territory Getty Images That's as close as Dan Hurley has gotten to a T all night. He, notably, said yesterday that he's never been T'ed up in his NCAA Tournament career... but another outburst like that and his streak might get snapped.Dan Hurley is HOT and he's giving the refs an earful after that call. The first one walked away and the second briefly engaged with him before the Huskies' coach entered his team's huddle.Ball brings sharpshooting to Final FourYa know who does like shooting in a dome? Solo Ball. The UConn guard was on the struggle bus, shooting 3 for 21 from 3-point range during the NCAA Tournament. He's 3 for 7 from deep tonight. Getty Images UConn runs beautiful offense. Chasing Alex Karaban and Braylon Mullins around screens isn't fun.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUConn holds major 3-point advantageH2 11:49 – UConn 52, Illinois 42UConn has finally committed a couple turnovers, but its 3-point shooting is still hot.The Huskies record their 10th 3-pointer of the evening on a Solo Ball triple. Meanwhile, Illinois has made just four of its 17 attempts from long range.In my attempt to click “start” and “stop” as accurately as possible, it appears as though that ball sat on the rim for 2.16 seconds. That’s a long time. Getty Images The officiating has been, uh, inconsistent thus far in the second half. I'm a fan of letting them play at this stage, but don't swallow the whistle if you were calling the types of fouls you were earlier this half!Absolutely wild — and impressive! — that UConn went almost 27 minutes without a turnover (and still hasn't had a live ball turnover.)
